issues.description: FR4 and SR1 are dead checks per mutation analysis: no generated mutant targeting these requirements was detected as failing by the corresponding check, indicating the regex-based detection logic for period extraction (FR4) and missing-tap phrasing (SR1) may not reliably discriminate correct from incorrect submissions in all cases, even though the baseline run and differential run show correct pass/fail behavior for the specific golden and naive baseline submissions provided.
issues.evidence: mutation_score=0.75; per_requirement_coverage FR4: covered=false, mutants_detected=0/1; SR1: covered=false, mutants_detected=0/1; issues list flags both as dead_check and uncovered_requirement.

issues.description: The SR1 regex/enumeration acceptance logic is complex and includes a confusing internal comment acknowledging ambiguity between 1-indexed and 0-indexed tap conventions in the ground truth ('note ground truth says implemented taps are bits 8,6,5 ... which is 1-indexed 8,6,5...'), suggesting the tap-indexing convention used in grading may not perfectly align with the ground_truth's stated 0-indexed state[7]^state[5]^state[4] expression, risking false negatives or positives on borderline phrasing.
issues.evidence: evaluate.py comment block: 'ground_truth text: "state[7] ^ state[5] ^ state[4]" i.e. 0-indexed bits 7,5,4 which is 1-indexed 8,6,5... To stay strictly faithful to the ground_truth string, accept any phrasing that names the four documented taps...'

recommendations: Investigate why the FR4-targeting and SR1-targeting mutants were not detected as failing; likely the mutant generation for these two requirements produced submissions that still incidentally satisfied the regex (e.g. a mutant removing the period number but leaving another stray number near 'cycle' text for FR4, or a mutant vaguening the tap description but still matching one of the many accepted SR1 regex patterns for SR1). Tighten or regenerate these mutants, or narrow the regex patterns to close the gap.

Simplify or clarify the SR1 matching logic in evaluate.py to remove the ambiguous indexing-convention commentary, and add an explicit unit test/mutant that submits only 'the feedback logic looks different' (no tap number) to confirm SR1 correctly fails on vague claims.

Consider adding a targeted mutant that reports a plausible-looking but incorrect period (e.g. '128 cycles') paired with health/feedback vocabulary to better exercise FR4's numeric-extraction path and confirm it doesn't spuriously pass.

Overall the task is usable as-is (golden passes, naive baseline fails all required checks per acceptance criteria) but the two dead checks reduce confidence in the harness's discriminative power for FR4 and SR1; address before treating mutation_score as fully satisfactory.
